name: Dossier holds many dated events
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AAS tablet Aegyptus 08, 264 11 (CDLI 100212, Ur III Umma) is one balanced account: a capital of worker-days, a blank, then several expenditure lines each with its own giri3 conveyor, a szunigin total, and a la2-ia3 deficit. One physical file contains many events. The ranker treats a chat session as one event: when is_event_sequence is set, max_per_session_top5 is the literal 1 (retrieval.rs:5619-5625) and a later turn of that session is dropped at the session_capped continue (5676-5679). This rule adds a predicate at that continue. A candidate whose terminal integer differs from every already selected turn of the same session is not capped. The literal 1 is not edited, so two turns that share the terminal integer still collapse. No speaker test.
math_formula: exempt(ti) = is_event_sequence AND terminal(ti) != 0 AND forall sj in selected, same session: terminal(sj) != terminal(ti); session_capped fires only when count >= 1 AND NOT exempt
rust_sketch:
let exempt = it.is_event_sequence && ix.turns[ti].terminal_digit != 0 && selected_turns.iter().filter(|j| ix.turns[**j].session == sess).all(|j| ix.turns[*j].terminal_digit != ix.turns[ti].terminal_digit);
if session_capped && !exempt { continue; } // retrieval.rs:5676. The literal 1 at 5619-5625 is not written.
funnel: S1-001 RECALL/INDEX: BEAM T@1 156→188; BEAM T@5 238→263; BEAM T@10 267→284; BEAM All@5 118→157; BEAM All@10 138→177
dedupe_note: Petrie seriation (turn1 #25) re-ranks sessions to maximize session-timestamp span and reads session dates. This never reads session_ts. Florilegium (turn1 #26) and the shipped cap keep one turn per session; this is an exemption, not a new quota. Catch-lines (turn1 #22) link the tail of session s to the head of a later session. This stays inside one session.

name: Deficit is capital minus expenditure
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AAS 013 (CDLI 100001) closes with si-i3-tum nig2-ka9-ak, the remainder of the balanced account, and names a year. Aegyptus 08, 264 11 (CDLI 100212) labels a la2-ia3 line after the expenditures. The remainder is an integer relationship between two sides, not a third commodity the query has to share tokens with. At ingest, while feats are built (3125-3272), store each already-parsed integer in the section it sits in. The deficit integer is emitted as an inheritable feat equal to the decimal string of |sum(section 0) - sum(section 1)|. A query whose only numeral is that deficit hits the turn even when the turn's prose never repeats the query's other nouns. Ranking reads the integer columns, not the body. This does not claim that the broken arithmetic on 100212 balances; the labels are what was read.
math_formula: deficit = sum(integers in section 0) - sum(integers in section 1); emit feat decimal(deficit) inheritable
dedupe_note: Step 32 trial balance requires every query group to be credited in the turn or its uptake. This is integer subtraction, not group coverage. Stocktaking residual (turn1 #23) down-weights query terms already satisfied. Khipu summation (turn1 #24) maximizes distinct (noun, numeral) pairs and does not touch slot 0. Sexagesimal composition (ancient #25) parses place value; these integers are already parsed. Primary-aggregate (ancient #32) prefers a turn with fewer digits; this emits a new digit.

name: Blank line splits capital from outlay
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AAS 065 (CDLI 100053) puts the silver capital, then the line $ blank space, then sza3-bi-ta, then the commodity lines. Co-occurrence that crosses that blank joins the capital to an expenditure it does not belong to, and a multi-hop query then retrieves the wrong side. At ingest a blank line increments the section index. Feats of section 0 are not inheritable onto tokens of section 1, and a content-token pair is not stored when the two tokens have different section indexes. Petuchah-style best-section coverage is a different operation and is not what this does: coverage is not replaced by the best section's coverage. The two sections stay two bags.
math_formula: cooccur(a, b) is stored iff section(a) == section(b); blank line increments section
rust_sketch:
let mut section: u32 = 0;
for line in lines { if line_is_blank(line) { section += 1; continue; } digit_cols.push((section, n)); } // 3125-3272. No feat id is shared across section.
dedupe_note: Petuchah/setumah (ancient #38) sets the turn's coverage to its best section. This refuses cross-section feats and does not take a max. Turin lacuna (ancient #11) drops df=0 query groups. Abusir header inheritance (ancient #16) copies a header onto cells.

name: Price is the next line's integer
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: On AAS 065 each commodity line is followed by a ku3-bi line, its silver. The price is the integer on the immediately following line, not a nearby integer anywhere in the turn. A query that carries two integers matches the turn only when those two integers occupy adjacent lines inside the same section. The pair is stored as an ordered feat (quantity, price). A turn that contains both integers on non-adjacent lines does not receive the pair feat, so it loses to the turn that does when the query has both.
math_formula: pair(q, p) iff line(p) == line(q)+1 AND section(q) == section(p); query with two integers requires the pair feat
rust_sketch: if let (Some(q), Some(p)) = (line_int[i], line_int[i+1]) { if sec[i]==sec[i+1] { pairs.insert((q, p)); } } // DetHashSet, ingest 3125-3272
dedupe_note: Ana approximation (ancient #41) matches a digit within plus or minus 10 percent. This is exact adjacency of two integers. Digit-unit split (ancient #24) splits 5km into 5 and km. No unit suffix is split here.

name: Slash fraction binds to the previous integer
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AAS 065 writes 1/2(disz), 1/3(disz), and 5/6(disz) on the silver lines. The fraction is orthographic, a token matching digits, a slash, and digits. It composes with the integer on the same line or the previous line by exact rational arithmetic: value = whole + num/den, reduced in integers. The composed numerator and denominator are both emitted. A query integer matches the numerator of that reduced value, not a window around it. No fraction word list.
math_formula: if token matches ^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$, value = prev_int * den + num, emit (value, den) in lowest terms
rust_sketch: if let Some((n, d)) = slash_fraction(tok) { let v = prev * d + n; let g = gcd(v, d); emit((v/g, d/g)); } // integers only, ingest
dedupe_note: Ana ±10% (ancient #41) is a tolerance. Sexagesimal composition (ancient #25) folds place-value words. This is an exact N/M token already written with a slash. Number-word composition is not reused.

name: Worker-days are the product of two integers
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AAS 013 and AAS 022 (CDLI 100010) open with a crew integer and a day integer on one line (AAS 022: 3(u) 4(disz) gurusz u4 1(disz)-sze3, 34 workers for 1 day). The labor total a query asks for is the product, which is often not written as its own token. At ingest, two integers on the same line emit their product as an inheritable feat. A query whose numeral equals that product matches the line. The factors stay available for a query that names one of them. Ranking never multiplies raw text; it reads the stored product.
math_formula: if a line holds exactly two integers a, b and a later line does not already equal a*b, emit feat a*b
rust_sketch: if ints.len()==2 { let p = ints[0].saturating_mul(ints[1]); products.push(p); } // i64, feat at 3125-3272
dedupe_note: Khipu (turn1 #24) covers distinct pairs across sessions and leaves slot 0 alone. This emits one integer, the product, onto the turn that holds the factors. Digit-unit split is not involved. Step 32 is group balance, not multiplication.

name: Year-name clause is the event key
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
target_slices: LOC Temporal; LME temporal-reasoning; BEAM temporal_reasoning
mechanism: LB 0068 (CDLI 388630) ends with mu ki-masz{ki} ba-hul, a year-name, after the barley receipt. The event's time is that closing clause, not the session timestamp and not a month-name lookup. At ingest the token-id sequence of the last non-blank line is stored as year_key. The ordering seat, a new function after apply_c2_step33_triangulation (algos_c2.rs:2593) called at retrieval.rs:6265-6272, sorts event-sequence candidates by the first-seen ordinal of year_key in the corpus, then by turn index. session_ts is not read. The seat runs for user/assistant transcripts; it does not return on is_event_sequence.
math_formula: order by first_seen[year_key] ascending, then turn index; first_seen is the minimum turn index in corpus order that carries that key
dedupe_note: Astronomical-diary calendar match (turn1 #32) multiplies a session score when a month-name window contains the session timestamp. This does not read month names or session_ts. Regnal anchoring (turn1 #41) retrieves an anchor event and ranks by date distance. This sorts by the ordinal of a stored suffix, one pass. Incipit (turn1 #31) weights the first user turn as a title. This uses the last line.

name: Year-after depth is a repetition count
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
target_slices: LOC Temporal; LME temporal-reasoning; BEAM event_ordering
mechanism: CUSAS 39, 153 (CDLI 250483) dates wages with mu us2-sa ki-masz{ki} ba-hul mu us2-sa-bi: the year after the year-after, depth 2, and the work is u4 1-kam. AAS 103 (CDLI 100090) has a single mu us2-sa. Depth is the count of a closed-class follower (after / following) in the date clause, not a regnal table. The seat orders by (base year_key ordinal, depth). Two turns with the same year formula and depths 0 and 2 sort in that order even when their session timestamps run the other way. The constant weights in the ranker are untouched.
math_formula: depth = count of closed-class {after, following} in the terminal clause; sort key (first_seen[year_key], depth, turn index)
rust_sketch:
let depth: u32 = terminal_tokens.iter().filter(|t| *t == AFTER || *t == FOLLOWING).count() as u32;
list.sort_by_key(|ti| (ord[year_key], ix.turns[*ti].year_depth, *ti)); // seat at 6265-6272
dedupe_note: Regnal event-anchored dating (turn1 #41) is a two-pass retrieval against session dates. Harris matrix is an edge topology. This is a repetition count of one closed-class word plus the year-key ordinal from S1-007's column. Torrens latest-wins is not used: a higher depth sorts later only relative to the same year key, and a different year key uses first-seen order, which can be earlier in the corpus.

name: A strict subset copy yields
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
target_slices: LOC Single-Hop; LME single-session-assistant; LME multi-session; BEAM summarization
mechanism: AAS 103 (CDLI 100090) rolls a second seal and labels it gaba-ri-dam, it is a copy. A later turn whose content-token set is a strict subset of an earlier turn in the same session, and which adds no integer the longer turn lacks, loses slot 1 to the longer turn. The seat is the new function at retrieval.rs:6265-6272. It does not use Jaccard, and it does not compare user turns with assistant turns. Speaker strings are not read. If the short turn carries an integer the long turn does not, it is not a copy and it stays.
math_formula: yield if content(short) strict-subset content(long) AND integers(short) subset integers(long) AND same session AND index(short) > index(long)
rust_sketch:
let sub = short.content.is_subset(&long.content) && short.ints.is_subset(&long.ints) && short.idx > long.idx;
if sub && list[0] == short_ti { list.swap(0, long_pos); } // DetHashSet, seat at 6265-6272
dedupe_note: Palimpsest diff (turn1) uses Jaccard plus a diff token. Asteriskos (ancient Hexapla) keeps a verbatim context mark. Source-superset realloc is a user/assistant seat already shipped. This is strict subset of content ids plus integer-set inclusion, speaker-agnostic, same session only.

name: A seal binds only the line above it
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: AfO 40-41, 55 3 (CDLI 100298) rolls a seal (kiszib3 ib2-ra) against one consignment, after that consignment's ki-la2-bi weight, not against the whole tablet. A line that is only a seal mark, detected as a line whose tokens are a closed-class seal shape or a line that is a single mid-turn caption after a blank, attaches its scope to the previous line's integer and entities. Those entities inherit the integer. Entities on earlier lines do not. A query naming the sealed party hits the sealed line's integer and misses the other lines' integers.
math_formula: if line i is a seal line, bind entities(line i-1) to int(line i-1) and to no other line's int
rust_sketch: if seal_line(i) { if let Some(n) = line_int[i-1] { for e in &line_ents[i-1] { sealed.insert((*e, n)); } } } // DetHashSet at ingest
dedupe_note: Notarial attestation (turn1 #40) multiplies turns by a named speaker. This does not read the speaker field. Household binding (Liye, ancient list) attaches a possessive to the nearest entity. This attaches one line, the previous line, and only when the current line is a seal line. Abusir red-stroke status (ancient #50) emits done/todo from checklist glyphs.

name: The median name is the controller
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Old Akkadian (CDLI period)
mechanism: WO 13, 08 (CDLI 217459) names a merchant, then the controller (lugal-gigir-e maszkim), then di-til-la. The controller is neither the first title-case token nor the last. BIN 08, 015 (CDLI 10012) puts maszkim-bi on the field that was given. When a clause has exactly three title-case tokens, the middle one is stored as the controller feat and the two endpoints are stored as parties. A query whose sole title-case token equals the middle one retrieves this turn by that feat. A query that names an endpoint does not receive the controller feat. No word list of offices.
math_formula: if title_case_count(clause) == 3, controller = token[1], parties = {token[0], token[2]}
rust_sketch: if caps.len()==3 { ctrl.insert(caps[1]); ends.insert(caps[0]); ends.insert(caps[2]); } // DetHashSet, ingest 3125-3272
dedupe_note: Third-text arbitration votes a rare token from a third session. This is the median orthographic name inside one clause. Two-witness corroboration (turn1 #33) requires two attestations. Muster-roll (turn1 #50) fills slots 2-5 with distinct names. Hakirot (ancient #3) compares core-cue sets between turns.

name: The name in both the first and last clause prevails
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
target_slices: LOC Multi-Hop; LOC Single-Hop; LME multi-session
mechanism: ITT 3, 06575 (CDLI 111382) is a ditilla. One brother di-ta in-tak4, withdrew from the case; the name that stands in the opening and again in the disposition is the party who receives the field. The prevailing entity is the title-case token that occurs in clause 0 and in the last clause. A token that occurs only in the opening is the party who left, and it is not given the verdict feat. The query matches the verdict feat. This is not 'the later turn wins': both clauses are inside one turn, and a name that appears only at the end does not prevail unless it also opened.
math_formula: prevail = title_case(clause_0) intersect title_case(clause_last); withdraw = title_case(clause_0) - prevail
rust_sketch:
let prevail: DetHashSet<u32> = first.intersection(&last).copied().collect();
for e in &prevail { feats.push(verdict_feat(e)); } // ingest, no body read at rank time
funnel: S1-012 RECALL/INDEX: LME T@1 350→375; LOC T@1 796→1049
dedupe_note: Torrens supersession seats the latest record. This requires membership in both endpoints of one turn. Damnatio and sanis-menu are different seats already rejected or shipped. Step 33 triangulation requires two score sightlines and a term cover; this is a set intersection of two clauses.

name: Names between the oath and the date are not events
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: The Nippur slave sale ArOr 07, 8 1 (CDLI 101851) states the price, the sale, nu-gi4-gi4-da, the oath mu lugal-bi i3-pa3, then lu2-inim-ma-bi-me and the witness names, and only then the month and the year. The witness block is not an event sequence. Tokens that sit after the last content clause and before the terminal integer are marked witness_zone at ingest. The ordering seat ignores witness_zone tokens when it decides which turn states the event. A turn that is only a witness list, no terminal integer outside that zone, cannot take slot 1 over a turn that has a terminal integer.
math_formula: witness_zone = tokens after the last clause boundary and before the terminal integer; event_key ignores that span
rust_sketch: if turn.terminal_digit == 0 && turn.witness_only { score_as_event = 0; } // seat at 6265-6272, column set at ingest
funnel: S1-013 ORDERING: LOC T@1 796→988; BEAM T@1 156→163
dedupe_note: Method of loci (turn1 #8) walks the k-th bullet. This deletes a zone from the order; it does not pick a k-th item. Profession-list status is a separate rule (S1-034) for a digit-free list that has no date zone at all. Two-witness corroboration is not applied.

name: The terminal integer is the date, earlier integers are quantities
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
target_slices: BEAM event_ordering; LOC Temporal; LME temporal-reasoning
mechanism: On the sale (CDLI 101851) the price integer is medial and the year stands after the witnesses. On LB 0068 (CDLI 388630) the year-name is the last line. When a turn has two or more integers, the one in the last eight tokens is the date key and every earlier integer is a quantity. The ordering seat sorts by the date key only. A quantity that happens to be numerically larger does not sort later. Turns with a single integer use that integer as the date key only when it sits in the last eight tokens; otherwise the turn has no date key and loses slot 1 to a turn that has one.
math_formula: date_key = last integer whose token offset is within 8 of the end, if any earlier integer exists or this is the only integer in that window; else none
rust_sketch:
let date_key = ints.iter().rev().find(|n| n.offset + 8 >= len).map(|n| n.value);
list.sort_by_key(|ti| (date_key(*ti).unwrap_or(i64::MAX), *ti)); // seat 6265-6272
dedupe_note: Loci picks the k-th list item. Inline date tokens (retrieval.rs:1452-1619) parse ISO and month names; this seat does not call that function and does not add month names. Diary calendar match (turn1 #32) uses session timestamps. This sorts an integer already on the turn.

name: An oath clause adds no event
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: The sale's oath, mu lugal-bi i3-pa3, is a clause whose only content token is one title-case name. It is the swearer, not a thing that happened in the order. A clause with exactly one title-case token and no integer is marked oath_zone. The ordering seat does not let an oath_zone clause supply slot 1, and its token does not count as a distinct event inside the turn. Clauses that have an integer or two title-case tokens stay.
math_formula: oath(clause) iff title_case_count == 1 AND integer_count == 0; event clauses are the complement
rust_sketch:
let oath = clause.caps.len()==1 && clause.ints.is_empty();
if oath { continue; } // seat walks clauses, 6265-6272
funnel: S1-015 ORDERING: LOC T@1 796→988; BEAM T@1 156→163
dedupe_note: Epistolary formula-length exclusion drops a high-df first or last sentence from BM25 length. This zeroes a clause by an orthographic count (one title-case, no integer), not by document frequency, and only for the event order. Ezib (ancient #18, same tradition, different tablet family) zeroes excluded query tokens under except/besides. This is not an exclusion cue.

name: A doubled verb under negation is not a second event
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Ur III (CDLI period; PeriodO https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmj72p.json labels Ur III 2100-2000 B.C.)
mechanism: The sale writes nu-gi4-gi4-da, a negated reduplicated verb: it shall not be returned. The reduplication is one legal act's refusal, not two returnings. A clause whose content tokens are a negation plus a token that is the same stem twice (orthographic doubling, or a hyphenated repeat) contributes zero events. The sale itself remains the event. The seat drops that clause before ordering.
math_formula: if clause has a closed-class negation and a token equal to its own double, event_count(clause) = 0
rust_sketch:
let doubled = toks.windows(2).any(|w| w[0]==w[1]) || toks.iter().any(|t| t.contains('-') && t.split('-').collect::<Vec<_>>()[0]==t.split('-').nth(1).unwrap_or(""));
if negated && doubled { return 0; }
dedupe_note: Dittography (Step 26) collapses two identical turns. This is one clause inside a turn. Compound-verb unit (ancient #10, šu ba-ti) emits a particle feat and halves the bare verb. This does not look at a particle class and does not halve a weight; the clause contributes no event.

name: The completion clause holds the price
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Old Babylonian (CDLI period). Two PeriodO authorities disagree (https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmk34f.json is 1800-1700 B.C.; https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p0njrb45vw3.json is 2004-ca.1780 B.C.), so the era follows the tablet.
mechanism: The orchard sale YBC 05336 (CDLI 306421) states sa10 til-la-ni-sze3, the price in full, in-na-an-la2, he paid, then the no-contest clause and the witnesses. The price integer is the integer in the clause that also contains a closed-class completion word (full, complete, paid). Other integers in the turn are not the price. The completion-clause integer is the feat a 'how much' query matches. The English closed class is the completion set already appropriate to closed-class grammar (full, complete, paid), not a list of commodities.
math_formula: price = integer in the unique clause that contains a token from {full, complete, paid}; if two such clauses, no price feat
rust_sketch:
let hits: Vec<i64> = clauses.iter().filter(|c| c.closed.iter().any(|w| COMPLETION.contains(w))).filter_map(|c| c.int).collect();
if hits.len()==1 { price = hits[0]; } // ingest
dedupe_note: Primary-aggregate prefers the turn with a single digit over a summary. This picks a clause inside one turn by a closed-class word. WH-slot voter is not used; there is no who/what branch. Kelal u-ferat is a general-then-specific legal reading and is not this.

name: Neighbors count only in order
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Old Babylonian (CDLI period). Two PeriodO authorities disagree (https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmk34f.json is 1800-1700 B.C.; https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p0njrb45vw3.json is 2004-ca.1780 B.C.), so the era follows the tablet.
mechanism: The same sale identifies the orchard by da X, da Y, u3 da Z: an ordered chain of neighbors, not a bag of names. Two query entities match the turn only when they occur in that order, with at most one token between them, and a closed-class coordinator (and) if a third name sits in the chain. Unordered co-occurrence is not enough, so a turn that mentions both people in a witness list does not take the location. The chain is stored as an ordered triple of entity ids.
math_formula: match iff exists i: entity[i]==q1 AND entity[i+1]==q2 AND offset(i+1)-offset(i) <= 2
rust_sketch: for w in ents.windows(2) { if w[1].off - w[0].off <= 2 { chains.insert((w[0].id, w[1].id)); } } // DetHashSet of ordered pairs, ingest
dedupe_note: Hollerith (Step 30) indexes an unordered co-occurrence pair. Cartouche (ancient list) treats a consecutive title-case span as one name. This requires order and a gap of at most one token, and it stores a pair of already-separate entities. Khipu two-hop (turn1 #42) pulls a bridge token into a second session.

name: An every-period integer is a cycle, not a date
tradition: Mesopotamian / Ancient Near East administrative, legal, and astronomical records
era: Old Babylonian (CDLI period). Two PeriodO authorities disagree (https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p047fhmk34f.json is 1800-1700 B.C.; https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p0njrb45vw3.json is 2004-ca.1780 B.C.), so the era follows the tablet.
mechanism: PBS 08/2, 116 (CDLI 262151) has four brothers give their nadītu sister a ration mu-am3, every year: barley, oil, and wool, as a periodic annuity rather than one transfer. A digit tied to a closed-class every/each plus a time-unit token is a period, not a point date. The ordering seat places that turn once per distinct clause that carries the period, in clause order, and does not also sort it by session_ts. A one-shot turn with a terminal date still sorts by its date key. The annuity does not compete with dated events as if it were a single day.
